impact: The 4000 ms deadline, the 60-80 s computation, the never-promoted private result and the requirement that every caller answer by the deadline cannot coexist: waiting violates the deadline, cancelling means a cold computation never succeeds, and detaching lets a short-lived MCP or CLI process exit on EOF and kill the only computation — while the never-promoted rule means finished work benefits nobody. FILED AS ISS-079 (critical) because it is a defect in the ticket's stated design. All three coherent resolutions are owner decisions and two of them route through the parked T-011: let the holder wait the measured pipeline bound (needs a durable result, contradicting never-promoted), own background computation in a persistent service (T-011), or promote an atomic cache result under shared writer authority (T-011's authority, and it makes the lease a correctness boundary rather than the optimization the ticket calls it).
resolution:
RESOLVED 2026-08-05, jointly with ISS-079 — this is the reviewer-lane filing of the same contradiction ISS-079 records in full (its own impact text says "FILED AS ISS-079 (critical)"), and it closes on the same evidence: the reader computation lease was CUT ENTIRELY by owner-delegated decision N-007 #4 (2026-08-04, .story/notes/N-007.json: "Readers never compute... cold computation belongs to the service alone... the 60-80s measured pipeline cost makes any in-band top-up a fiction for MCP clients that time out at 60s").

The 4000 ms deadline, the never-promoted private result, the answer-by-deadline rule and the herd machinery no longer exist in any binding document. Verified in the tree: T-013's ticket (.story/tickets/T-013.json, repaired 2026-08-04 at twelve sites including the title) states "There is no lease, no lease port allocation, no `purpose` namespace, no wait deadline, no subprocess cap, no private temporary generation, and no herd contention"; AC 6 is "CUT (N-007 decision 4)" and its replacement requires an IMMEDIATE honest-stale answer with no computation started, plus a mutant test that MUST fail if reader-side compute reappears; Scope-out forbids reintroducing reader-side computation "in any form... as an optimization". The live plan (docs/t013-replan-n007-n008-rev3.md §2 map and :93) withdraws the base plan's lease sections and deletes "the 4000 ms deadline and the subprocess cap" by name. No current AC recreates the deadline-vs-cost tension: --cached (AC 7) spawns no ccusage subprocess, and no AC carries a wait deadline.

Of the three coherent resolutions this filing listed, the one taken is background computation owned by the persistent service — T-011 — which was UNPARKED 2026-08-05 (park discharged after commit 9524902 landed its blocking store items), so the resolution's home is a live ticket, not a parked one. Residuals are owned elsewhere: the honest-stale path's service-status signal is HELD on T-011's probe (ISS-086, reopened; readers report `undetermined`), and the base plan document docs/t013-mcp-server-plan.md retains the lease design as preserved-but-superseded reasoning whose withdrawal marker lives in rev3 §2 rather than in-file (housekeeping noted in ISS-079's resolution).

See ISS-079 for the full closure argument and tree citations.
